headline: A 2021 law lets the Drug Enforcement Administration bar certain repeat-problem businesses from registering to handle controlled substances, either temporarily or permanently.
what_it_does: The law gives the DEA authority to block an entity from registering to manufacture, distribute, or dispense controlled substances. This applies when the entity meets a condition that could justify suspending or revoking its registration and has a history of prior suspensions or revocations. The bar can be temporary or permanent.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses and other entities registered with the DEA to make, distribute, or dispense controlled substances
who_it_affects.how: Entities with a history of prior DEA suspensions or revocations could be denied or kept from getting a registration if they meet a suspension or revocation condition.

who_it_affects.group: Entities seeking a new DEA registration to handle controlled substances
who_it_affects.how: Applicants with a prior suspension or revocation history may be barred from registering, either for a set period or permanently.

when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not give a separate effective date. The law was enacted on August 6, 2021.
